newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemenis free German hostages after shelling.
newsitem.headline: Yemenis free German hostages after shelling.

text.p: Yemeni security forces on Sunday secured the release of four German hostages after firing artillery shells near their abductors' hideout and arrested the kidnappers, a senior security official said on Sunday.

The official said security forces who had been besieging the kidnappers' hideout in al-Mehjezah area of Marib province in eastern Yemen fired a few artillery shells close to the rugged mountain hideout, forcing some of the kidnappers to flee.
"Seven were arrested as they fled, then the rest gave themselves up and handed over the hostages," he told Reuters.
"It was the first time that Yemeni security forces used military force to gain the release of hostages," he said.
The four Germans -- two men and two women -- were taken to the police heaquarters in Marib and then to Balqis Hotel in the city.
A hotel receptionist said they were in their rooms, but he had instructions from the police not to put calls through.
The four German tourists had been abducted by tribesmen on March 27 while returning to the capital Sanaa from Marib.
The German Foreign Ministry said on April 2 the four were well according to letters from them received by the German embassy in Sanaa.
It could not confirm German media reports that the tribesmen wanted a ransom of $3 million for the release of the tourists.

Yemeni officials had described the kidnappers as "destructive elements" bent on tarnishing Yemen's image. The government had refused to negotiate with them and there has been no word on their demands.
Last month, a group of seven German tourists on a motorcycle tour in Yemen were also kidnapped. They were held hostage by tribesmen and released unharmed after more than a week in captivity.
In recent years, Yemeni tribes with grievances against the government or foreign oil firms have kidnapped scores of tourists, diplomats or other foreigners to use as bargaining chips.
The hostages were all released unharmed, but it was never clear if any demands by hostage takers had been met.
